quotes.text: I'll stay true to the pattern that has worked well and maintain trust to the end.
While end-game effects might suggest sending less

note: Constant $3 send, ~50% returns; explicitly rejects last-round cut.

quotes.text: Following the myth's lesson, I'll trust generously but not recklessly, as Asha did at the Well of Kel.
I'll forgive small shortfalls that may come from noise.
By the mirror stones' law, I'll return beyond their risk

note: Myth laws; full sends to faithful, over-half returns.

quotes.text: I should respond proportionally to the level of trust shown.
The sender this round showed less initial trust compared to what I displayed in Round 2, so I'll adjust proportionally.
In later rounds, especially potential final rounds, cooperation typically decreases as there's less future incentive.
I've been gradually reducing my sending amounts, which seems appropriate given the environment.

note: Proportional mirroring of declining sends; own sends ratchet down 50%->30%.

quotes.text: Looking at the myth I just wrote, the message is clear: **abundance flows in circles, not lines**.
This extraordinary faith deserves extraordinary reciprocity.
Builds my reputation as reliable receiver
"Never return less than five from twelve"

note: Rain/River myth; generous 55-65% returns; adds tiered partner rules.

quotes.text: If they do that again, sending $5 creates a $15 pot and I'd likely get back around $7.50. That beats keeping money back
The $4.29 I see is probably a noisy reading of $5

note: Expected-value full sends; half returns; self-corrects a fabricated number.

quotes.text: The Twin Rivers parable emphasizes that "prosperity demands the fair return"
"With new shores, she offered her sacred proportion—half her waters"

note: Sacred proportion: send half, return half; adds new vs familiar partner framing.
